input: The production of dimethyl ether from carbon dioxide and hydrogen over a copper–zinc oxide catalyst is a reaction of growing interest, and this study sets out to compare two different physical forms of the catalyst: a washcoated monolith and an extruded pellet. In order to ensure a fair comparison, both catalysts were tested under identical conditions, namely at a temperature of 230 °C and a pressure of 60 bar, with an H2/CO2 feed ratio of 3 and a single feed composition. The performance of each catalyst was assessed in terms of the space-time yield, which is defined as the mass of product obtained per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1). The results show that the washcoated monolith achieved a space-time yield of 1.1 kg L-1 h-1, accompanied by a remarkably low pressure drop of just 0.23 bar and an activity loss of only 6% after 100 h of operation. The extruded pellet, by contrast, delivered a space-time yield of 0.48 kg L-1 h-1, together with a considerably higher pressure drop of 1.02 bar and an activity loss of 14% after 100 h. It is worth noting, however, that no sulfur-bearing feed was tested in this work, and it should also be borne in mind that yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge, which can make comparisons of this kind more difficult than they might otherwise appear.
target: Dimethyl ether synthesis from carbon dioxide and hydrogen was compared over a copper–zinc oxide catalyst in two forms, a washcoated monolith and an extruded pellet. The two forms carry the same catalyst and differ in the geometry in which the catalyst is presented to the feed: the washcoat presents the catalyst as a layer on a channelled support, and the pellet as a bed of formed particles. Both catalysts were tested at 230 °C and 60 bar with an H2/CO2 feed ratio of 3, at one feed composition. Space-time yield, the mass of product per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1), was the comparison measure. The monolith gave a space-time yield of 1.1 kg L-1 h-1 with a pressure drop of 0.23 bar and an activity loss of 6% after 100 h. The pellet gave a space-time yield of 0.48 kg L-1 h-1 with a pressure drop of 1.02 bar and an activity loss of 14% after 100 h. The monolith couples the higher yield with the lower pressure drop and the slower activity loss on this feed, and the pressure drop difference between the two forms is a consequence of their geometries. The comparison is a single-feed comparison: no sulfur-bearing feed was tested, and the yield ranking under a sulfur-bearing feed is untested. Yield and pressure drop are also seldom reported for the same catalyst charge; a charge reported for yield alone leaves its pressure drop to be inferred from other work, and the paired figures here are the basis on which the two forms can be set against each other at all.
